Package express.mvp.roray.ffm.utils.memory

package express.mvp.roray.ffm.utils.memory
Binary, zero-copy codecs built on the Java Foreign Function & Memory API.

This package provides sequential readers and writers over MemorySegment for high-throughput encoding/decoding without intermediate heap copies.

Core Utilities

  • BinaryReader - Sequential, zero-copy decoding API for primitives, VarInts, strings, and slices
  • BinaryWriter - Sequential, fluent, zero-copy encoding API for primitives, VarInts, strings, and slices
  • SegmentBinaryReader - MemorySegment-backed BinaryReader implementation
  • SegmentBinaryWriter - MemorySegment-backed BinaryWriter implementation

Flyweight & Views

  • FlyweightAccessor - Contract for reusable flyweights that wrap a segment and expose structured field access
  • Utf8View - Zero-allocation flyweight view over a UTF-8 slice of a MemorySegment
  • BitSetView - Zero-allocation BitSet-like view for bit operations over a segment slice

Layouts & Helpers

  • Layouts - Predefined unaligned, endian-aware ValueLayout constants for packed IO
  • SegmentUtils - Stateless utilities for operating on MemorySegments (e.g., CRC32)
  • VarFieldWriter - Builder for messages with variable-length fields addressed by offset/length headers

Pooling

  • MemorySegmentPool - Thread-safe pool for reusable off-heap segments to reduce allocation and GC pressure
  • PooledSegment - Try-with-resources wrapper that returns a segment to its pool on close

Conventions

  • Endianness suffixes: BE for big-endian (network byte order) and LE for little-endian.
  • Variable-length integers: VarInt (32-bit) and VarLong (64-bit) use a 7-bit continuation encoding.
  • Strings and byte arrays are typically length-prefixed with a VarInt. For allocation-free string decoding, populate a Utf8View instead of creating a String.
  • Some APIs can return a slice view (MemorySegment) to avoid copying data to the heap.
